source.title: Fact Finding: Attempting to Reverse-Engineer Factual Recall on the Neuron Level (Post 1)

record.tranche_reason: The study examines neuron-level mechanisms in Pythia and reports evidence against a simple, localized neuron-by-neuron account of factual recall. It does not test the claim versions’ specific audits or attribution-graph method.
record.gate_note: The study reports neuron interventions and measurements relevant to whether individual neurons have coherent jobs, but does not measure the proportion of neuron poles with one or two jobs, audit explanations on held-out activations, or evaluate attribution graphs. Results about context truncation and other circuit details that do not bear on neuron job coherence are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study analyses neurons in Pythia 2.8B's early MLPs during athlete-sport recall. It reports no share of interpretable neurons, no neuron-level attribution graph, and no scoring of explanations against held-out activations. Its neuron findings are about one selected neuron and a distributed lookup, a different construct from any version. It also argues that superposition is the norm and that the lookup was not localisable to specific neurons, but it gives no result aimed at a version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also falsify the strong single-step detokenization and strong hash-and-lookup hypotheses. They state the lookup was not localisable to specific neurons. They take SAE successes as strong evidence that superposition is the norm, and they treat early MLPs as an uninterpretable lookup table best black-boxed.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates factual recall in Pythia 2.8B using probes, neuron interventions, and circuit analysis; it does not perform a neuron-pole job audit or test explanations on held-out activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Resample-ablating single neurons gave little correlation in their effects across different Michael Jordan facts. The authors take this as falsifying single-step detokenization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In factual recall, different facts about one entity rely on different neurons rather than on one shared set of lookup neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected neuron L5N6045 responds preferentially to baseball-player names, even after an orthogonal projection, but is not monosemantic on broader text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A neuron with a coherent task role can still respond to other, unrelated inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state the sport lookup is spread across MLPs 2 to 6 and 'not localisable to specific neurons or even a single layer'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Factual lookup in early MLPs is distributed across many neurons and layers, not carried by individually interpretable neurons.

record.problems: The neuron-level example is a selected neuron, not a systematic sample or estimate of neuron-job prevalence. The study notes that it examined only 1,500 facts while each of the five studied MLP layers had 10,000 neurons, making the analysis underdetermined. The reported neuron results lack numerical effect sizes and uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed claim versions were identified.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and no shares of one-job, two-job or unknown poles.
Pythia 2.8B only. No estimate of neuron-job shares and no comparison across models, architectures or scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and no test of pose or recursive generalization.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools, and no interpretable-share estimates.
No neuron-based attribution graphs and no comparison with a trained replacement model.
No test of whether explanations drawn from activating examples predict firing on held-out text.
No automated simulation scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The Alignment Forum post is the main body of a 5-post sequence, and the neuron-level detail is in Post 3. Footnote 3 asserts, without numbers, that language-model neurons are less often monosemantic than image-model neurons. That stance runs against the essay's thesis but is not a measured result, so it gets no label. The reader's 'tests'/T5 classification is changed to discusses/T6.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimates of the shares of poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
The study examines Pythia 2.8B, but does not estimate neuron-job shares or compare models, architectures, or scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, interpretability tools, or estimated interpretability shares.
The study does not build or evaluate attribution graphs, or compare them with a trained replacement model.
No explanation is tested for its ability to predict neuron activations on held-out text.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text is reported.

rows.subject: Pythia 2.8B
rows.operation_detail: Resample-ablated individual neurons on the Michael Jordan input by replacing their activation with that from another athlete; measured effects on correct answers for multiple facts.

conditions.value: multiple facts known about Michael Jordan
one neuron at a time; activation resampled from 64 randomly selected other athletes

rows.measure: Correlation between each neuron's effect on pairs of facts
rows.value: Little correlation between effects across pairs of facts
rows.locator: What we learned about the MLPs / Post 3 Summary
rows.note: The text says this is evidence against the strong single-step detokenization hypothesis, which predicts the same neurons matter for each fact. No correlation values are given.
rows.check: Bears on whether single-step detokenization neurons serve all facts, not on neuron job shares. No correlation values are given.

rows.subject: Pythia 2.8B, L5N6045
rows.operation_detail: Measured the neuron's activation on athlete names.

conditions.value: names of athletes playing baseball, basketball, or football

rows.value: Activated significantly more on the names of baseball-playing athletes
rows.locator: What we learned about the MLPs / Post 3 Summary
rows.note: The study calls this a baseball neuron and says it composes directly with the fact-extracting head; it gives no numerical effect size.
rows.check: A single selected neuron (L5N6045), not a sample. No effect size is given.

rows.subject: Pythia 2.8B, L5N6045
rows.operation_detail: Projected each athlete's component orthogonal to the other 1,500 athletes onto the neuron.

conditions.value: component orthogonal to the other 1,500 athletes

rows.measure: Neuron activation by athletes' sport after projection
rows.value: Still fires more for baseball players than other players
rows.locator: What we learned about the MLPs / Post 3 Summary
rows.note: The authors say this may suggest the neuron also acts as a lookup table; no numerical values are given.
rows.check: Same selected neuron. This is about lookup-table behaviour, not explanation coverage. No numbers are given.

rows.subject: Pythia 2.8B, L5N6045
rows.operation_detail: Examined the neuron's activations on a broader data distribution.
rows.measure: Breadth and coherence of neuron activations
rows.value: Often activates on sport-related things, but is not monosemantic
rows.locator: What we learned about the MLPs / Post 3 Summary
rows.note: No activation examples, counts, or score are reported here.
rows.check: A qualitative remark ('not monosemantic') about one neuron, with no activation examples, counts or scores. It cannot stand for a population share.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
